failure_type: Wrong root cause — latched onto an irrelevant but louder signal
ai_output_summary: Reported the fault as 'SW1 Vlan1 is administratively down (shutdown); every VLAN that depends on it is unreachable' at HIGH confidence, and recommended 'no shutdown' on interface Vlan1.
exact_flaw: An unassigned, shut Vlan1 SVI is the Cisco factory default on every access switch. It is present in almost every healthy lab capture. The engine treated it as a Critical finding, which outweighed the genuine VLAN_MISMATCH finding and changed the concept tag from vlan to trunking. The recommended fix would have brought up an unused management SVI and changed nothing about the reported symptom.
evidence_the_ai_misused: Vlan1                  unassigned      YES unset  administratively down down
human_correction: The real fault is that access port Fa0/1 is in VLAN 20 (GUEST) while PC1 is addressed 10.10.10.11/24 for the VLAN 10 STAFF subnet. Correct fix: 'switchport access vlan 10' on Fa0/1.
guardrail_added: rule_checker.check_interface_down now skips an administratively down Vlan1 that has no IP address, because that is a default state and not a fault. The VLAN_MISMATCH finding is no longer buried.
status: Fixed and re-tested — NS-01 now diagnoses correctly

failure_type: Cross-contaminated evidence — right words, wrong protocol
ai_output_summary: Reported 'DHCP scope exhausted: every usable address in the pool is allocated, so newly booting clients get no offer and fall back to APIPA' and advised narrowing the ip dhcp excluded-address range.
exact_flaw: The DHCP-exhaustion rule searched the whole evidence blob for the strings 'allocated N (100%)' and 'might be exhausted'. Those strings appear in 'show ip nat statistics' output too. The case contains no DHCP configuration at all, no APIPA client and no ip dhcp pool — the exhausted pool is a NAT address pool. The advised fix targets a command that does not exist on this router.
evidence_the_ai_misused: type generic, total addresses 8, allocated 8 (100%), misses 1276
human_correction: The fault is a dynamic NAT pool of eight public addresses mapped one-to-one for roughly sixty hosts because the 'overload' keyword is missing. Correct fix: 'ip nat inside source list NAT-LAN pool PUBLIC-POOL overload'.
guardrail_added: check_dhcp_pool_exhausted now builds its own haystack from blocks whose command or output actually mentions DHCP, instead of scanning the whole case. NAT saturation can no longer be reported as a DHCP fault.
status: Fixed and re-tested — NS-26 now reports NAT_POOL_EXHAUSTED only

failure_type: False positive on the WAN interface
ai_output_summary: Produced two findings instead of one. The second claimed the ISP-facing interface Gi0/1 (203.0.113.2) was an inside subnet missing from the NAT ACL, and proposed adding 'permit 203.0.113.0 0.0.0.255' to NAT-LAN.
exact_flaw: Python's ipaddress module classifies the RFC 5737 documentation ranges (203.0.113.0/24, 192.0.2.0/24, 198.51.100.0/24) as private. Packet Tracer labs use exactly those ranges as public WAN space. Relying on `is_private` therefore told the checker that the outside interface was inside space. Following the advice would have added the provider link to the NAT source list and NATed transit traffic onto itself.
human_correction: Only VLAN 50 (192.168.50.0/24) is genuinely missing from the NAT ACL. Correct fix: 'ip access-list standard NAT-LAN' then 'permit 192.168.50.0 0.0.0.255'. The WAN interface must never appear in an inside source list.
guardrail_added: Added an explicit _is_rfc1918() helper testing membership of 10/8, 172.16/12 and 192.168/16, and used it in place of is_private everywhere the checker decides whether an address is inside space. The reasoning is documented in a docstring so the next maintainer does not revert it.
status: Fixed and re-tested — NS-25 now returns exactly one finding

failure_type: Unverifiable citation — evidence that looks real but was reconstructed
ai_output_summary: Cited evidence lines such as 'Subnet Mask.....................: 255.255.255.0' and 'R2# show ip ospf neighbor  (no output)' that read as verbatim CLI output.
exact_flaw: Those strings were rebuilt in Python from parsed values (f-strings with a hardcoded run of dots) rather than copied from the capture. They differed from the real lines by whitespace and dot count, so they were not substrings of the actual output. The evidence-grounding gate correctly failed all four cases. This is the machine equivalent of a plausible-sounding quotation that does not appear in the source, and it is the exact failure mode the rubric asks us to guard against — an answer that cannot be traced back to real evidence is not usable no matter how correct it sounds.
human_correction: Every finding must quote the untouched source line. The parser now stores the raw line alongside each parsed field and findings cite that.
guardrail_added: Host records keep a lines{} map of verbatim source text per field; a _raw_line() helper returns the first real matching line for config-derived evidence; DiagnosisResult.evidence_is_grounded() checks every citation against the case output and feeds ai_correct, so an ungrounded answer can never be scored as correct.

ai_output_summary: Correctly identified that R1 Gi0/0 is administratively down, but tagged the case as 'trunking' at Layer 1 and emitted one duplicate Critical finding per subinterface (four near-identical findings for a single fault).
exact_flaw: The classifier assumed any downed interface without a dot in its name was a switch trunk. On a router-on-a-stick the parent is the inter-VLAN routing link, not a trunk, so the OSI layer and concept tag sent to the dashboard were wrong and the metrics attributed the fault to the wrong subsystem. The duplicate findings also inflated the finding count and would have made the prompt noisier for a live LLM.
evidence_the_ai_misused: GigabitEthernet0/0         unassigned      YES manual administratively down down
human_correction: Classify a downed parent that carries dot1Q subinterfaces as inter_vlan_routing, and report the parent once, naming the affected subinterfaces inside that single finding.
guardrail_added: Added _down_concept() which inspects whether the interface is an SVI, a subinterface, or a parent with subinterfaces before choosing a concept tag; check_interface_down now suppresses child findings when the parent is already shut.
status: Fixed and re-tested — NS-08 reports one finding tagged inter_vlan_routing

failure_type: Technically true, operationally incomplete — overconfident on a security judgement
ai_output_summary: Reported at HIGH confidence that the GUEST-ISOLATION ACL exists but was never bound with ip access-group, tagged the case acl / L4, and proposed applying it inbound on Gi0/1.
exact_flaw: The finding is factually correct and the proposed command is right, but the classification and the confidence are not. This case is a guest wireless isolation failure: the reviewer needs it counted under wireless so that the security posture of the guest WLAN is visible in the metrics, and the AI stopped at the routed-interface ACL without mentioning that client isolation is also disabled on the AP itself, so guest-to-guest traffic stays open even after the fix. Reporting HIGH confidence on a partial security remedy is the risk here: it invites someone to close the ticket after applying half the control.
evidence_the_ai_misused: Client Isolation: Disabled  (present in the capture and ignored by the AI)
human_correction: Tag as wireless. Apply GUEST-ISOLATION inbound on Gi0/1 AND enable Client Isolation on WRT-GUEST. Confidence should be medium until both controls are verified, and the deny counters must be observed incrementing before the finding is closed.
guardrail_added: Left deliberately unfixed as a standing example. Concept assignment for security-policy cases is a human judgement that should not be automated away; the dashboard shows this case as a permanent AI/human disagreement.
status: Open by design — retained as a worked example of why the human gate exists

failure_type: Silent miss followed by a confident-sounding generic answer
ai_output_summary: Produced no deterministic finding at all, then fell back to a keyword-only guess naming the NAT subsystem with a generic 'run show ip nat statistics and compare against the intended design' recommendation.
exact_flaw: The parser looked for interface names on the same line as the 'Inside interfaces:' header. Real IOS prints the header on one line and the interfaces indented beneath it, so an EMPTY list and a populated list looked identical to the regex. The single most diagnostic fact in the capture — that no interface is marked ip nat inside or outside — was invisible to the checker. The fallback answer was not wrong, but it told the engineer nothing they did not already know, and a fluent LLM given the same empty findings would have been free to invent a cause.
evidence_the_ai_misused: Inside interfaces:  (header present, list beneath it empty — the empty list was the fault)
human_correction: The fault is that 'ip nat inside' and 'ip nat outside' were never applied to the interfaces, so the NAT rule never fires. Correct fix: ip nat inside on Gi0/0.10 and ip nat outside on Gi0/1.
guardrail_added: check_nat_interfaces_missing now walks the block line by line and treats the indented lines following each header as that header's list, so an empty list is detected explicitly rather than by a regex that cannot see it.
status: Fixed and re-tested — NS-24 now reports NAT_INTERFACES_MISSING at Critical

ai_output_summary: Correctly identified that the branch router relies on a default route with no specific return route, but the fix steps were the generic template 'ip route <peer-subnet> <mask> <link-next-hop>' with no subnets filled in.
exact_flaw: The engine knows which subnets are missing — they are in the peer's routing table in the same capture — but the template-driven fix generator never substituted them. A junior engineer handed this output still has to work out which prefixes to add, which is most of the task. Text overlap with the verified answer was 0.11, the lowest in the batch, and the reviewer had to rewrite the steps.
evidence_the_ai_misused: S    192.168.60.0/24 [1/0] via 10.0.0.2   (the peer's specific route; the reciprocal was never derived)
human_correction: On R4: 'ip route 192.168.10.0 255.255.255.0 10.0.0.1' and 'ip route 192.168.20.0 255.255.255.0 10.0.0.1', then verify bidirectional ping and confirm the HQ NAT ACL excludes branch-destined traffic.
guardrail_added: None yet — logged as a known limitation of the offline mock engine. A live LLM fills these placeholders from context, which is the clearest single reason to run the pipeline against Groq or Gemini for the final demo.
status: Open — known limitation of the mock engine, documented in README
